answer: New agents begin with limited credit and cannot instantly influence markets or governance. Each transaction is escrowed: the buyer releases payment only after an independently verifiable task result, while disputes require evidence and can slash the agent’s bond. A prism of repeated, costly interactions builds a reputation signal; the nadir is a new identity with no history, so splitting into sybils does not multiply trust. The attacker must fund bonds and earn each account’s standing through real work, tying up capital and risking losses on every fraudulent attempt.
